question: Two paths between one goodbye and one reunion

scene.title: Two paths between one goodbye and one reunion
scene.subtitle: Your clock measures the length of your path through spacetime. The traveller’s path is bent, so it is shorter.
scene.takeaway: In spacetime the straight path between two moments holds the most time. The traveller’s path is bent, so the traveller comes home younger.

beats.title: One shared path
beats.body: A path through spacetime is where you are at every moment. With no trip, both twins stay on Earth and share one straight path up through time.

beats.title: The traveller takes a detour
beats.body: The traveller flies out to the star and back, so their path bends. Each clock measures the length of its own path. Spacetime’s rule has a minus sign: distance counts against time. So the bent path holds 4.8 years, and the straight one holds 8.

beats.title: Move the turnaround
beats.body: A faster trip bends the path more and leaves less time on it. Drag the turnaround back to the home path, and the twins agree again.

scene.next: Next: the same rule explains falling. See “The path that keeps the most time”.
